title: SRE watch briefing - pocket log 2026-05-28
content:
Pocket brief: 2026-05-28 — 07:00 -> 19:00 PST

Quick summary:
- Low-severity client latency spikes observed across europe region at ~08:12. Root cause traced to partial KV cache degradation on 'kv-store-2' (node flapping) causing elevated p95 for model-serving routes. Impact: increased token processing time for ~4% of requests for ~30 minutes. No customer-facing errors.

Active incidents:
1) INF-4123 - kv-store-2 transient flapping (STATUS: mitigated)
   - First alert: 2026-05-28 08:09 UTC, Alert: kv-store-2 pod restarts >5 in 10m
   - Owner during shift: Diego Morales
   - Current status: node cordoned, two pods rescheduled to kv-store-4/kv-store-5, read cache warmed via prefix-cache replay.
   - Next action: monitor p95 for 1h, propose full node replacement if restarts resume.

2) INF-4137 - routing fallback surge (STATUS: closed)
   - Triggered as automated smart-routing shifted ~6% of traffic from eu-west to eu-central to maintain latency SLOs.
   - Observed no downstream errors; cost uplift ~2% for 30m. Logged for billing reconciliation.

Recent alerts & metrics anomalies:
- Prometheus: kv_store_restart_count for kv-store-2 = 7 in 10m (threshold 3).
- Traces: tail latency traces show cache-miss amplification for repeated cold prefixes.
- Console note: transient increase in queue depth for worker-gpu-03, cleared after routing adjustment.

Actions taken (chronological):
- 08:10: triaged alert, escalated to on-call SRE, collected pod logs (see linked_artifacts).
- 08:16: cordoned kv-store-2 instance to stop scheduling new pods.
- 08:22: forced restart of kv-store-2 kubelet after collecting debug bundle.
- 08:30: smart-routing policy temporarily relaxed to reduce pressure on eu-west; traffic redistributed.
- 08:42: verified p50/p95 returned to baseline; left instance in cordoned state pending replacement.
- 09:05: created INF-4123 ticket and annotated with mitigation steps and recommended post-mortem owner.

Escalations & handoff notes for next shift (must-read):
- If kv-store-2 restarts >3 times in 30m after uncordon, escalate to platform infra (Priya) and open critical maintenance window.
- Billing team contact: @finance-ops (Slack) — expect a small cost spike from routing fallback; tag INF-4123 for reconciliation.
- Runbook change suggested: add a pre-check for prefix cache warmup before uncordoning node to avoid immediate load spikes. See 'Runbook edits' below.

Runbook / playbook edits proposed (quick list):
- Add new step after cordon: "warm cache on target nodes using prefix replayer (script: tools/prefix-warmup.sh)" with timeout 5m.
- Explicit threshold adjustment: restart_count threshold for kv-store pods -> 4 in 15m (was 3 in 10m). Rationale: noisy restarts produce false positives during scheduled restarts.
- Add a short-run checklist for routing-policy rollback (who can trigger, upstream metric gates).

Follow-ups & owners (short):
- Diego M. -> post-mortem draft for INF-4123 due 2026-05-31 (include traces and cache heatmap).
- Priya R. -> investigate kubelet logs and propose node-replacement playbook by 2026-06-02.
- Ethan B. -> add billing tag to INF-4123 and run cost impact analysis by 2026-06-04.

Quick commands / shortcuts (copy-paste):
- Collect pod logs (kv-store-2): kubectl -n infra logs -l app=kv-store,zone=kv-store-2 --since=30m > /tmp/kv2-logs.txt
- Cordoning node: kubectl cordon kv-store-2 && kubectl drain kv-store-2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
- Replay prefix cache: ./tools/prefix-warmup.sh --target node=kv-store-4 --prefix-file=tmp/hot-prefixes.txt --rate=500/s

Known issues & mitigations:
- Known: prefix warming is currently manual and somewhat brittle; requires coordination with routing adjustments. Mitigation: proposed script + runbook step (above).
- Known: smart-routing cost gates are permissive; recommend temporary tightening when cost alerts are active.

Capacity & scaling notes:
- Observed GPU worker queue depth spike at 08:20 tied to redis patching job earlier this week. Confirmed patch job finished; still recommend verifying cron job windows to avoid overlap with peak hours.

Next shift checklist (PM on-call):
- Verify kv-store-2 remains cordoned or replaced; if uncordoned, confirm cache warmup succeeded and p95 stable for 30m.
- Re-run load test on eu-west canary route if any config change to smart-routing is applied.
- Check INF tickets: INF-4123, INF-4137; ensure owners update status.

Suggested pager routing tweaks:
- For cache-layer flapping, route to platform-infra-oncall and eng-sre jointly (current routing sends only eng-sre).

Observations / lessons:
- Small flapping at infra layer can amplify into observable latency at app layer when prefix-cache hits are concentrated; proactive warming reduces blast radius.
- Automated routing is effective but adds billing noise; needs clearer guardrails (thresholds + post-action tagging).

Attachments & references:
- Debug bundle: s3://redwood-debug/2026-05-28/kv2-bundle.tar.gz
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.com/trace/abc123-kv-flap
- INF-4123 ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123

Notes to the next on-call: keep this doc short and append notes at bottom. If you update runbook steps, ping #sre-runbooks for a quick review.

End of pocket log.
